tldr: A Nov 13 paper argued that SAE steering applied to every token pushes representations off-distribution and proposed per-token gating that follows the generation trajectory. A Nov 19 paper then recast RL post-training of diffusion transformers as activation steering, tying a costly training step to an inference-time intervention.
whats_new: A Nov 25 paper, TASK memory, pairs each text memory note with activation steering and a removable knowledge edit, reporting memory-ignoring errors cut to at most 1.5% across ten model-dataset cells on frozen LLMs.
why_it_matters: Activation steering is moving from a behavior knob into agent memory, so teams fighting memory hallucination on open-weight models get a no-fine-tuning option beyond better retrieval and prompting.

beats.headline: SAE steering moves from every token to trajectory-aware gating
beats.summary: Targets the off-distribution drift that always-on steering causes.

beats.headline: RL post-training in diffusion transformers recast as activation steering
TASK memory uses steering plus knowledge edits against memory hallucination
beats.summary: Moves steering from output control into how frozen LLMs use stored memories.

open_questions: How much generation quality does trajectory-aware gating recover compared with steering every token?
Can a steering vector reproduce the RL post-training gains in diffusion transformers without running RL?
What latency and storage cost does TASK memory add per stored memory compared with text-only notes?
Do TASK memory's removable knowledge edits stay isolated when many memories are active at once?
take_for_builders: If your agent ignores or misuses its stored notes on a frozen open-weight model, add a memory-ignoring error rate to your evals now so you can compare TASK-style steering against your current retrieval setup.
